evidence: The constructor in src/domain/product.ts checks the id, name and stock and throws DomainError if they are invalid. This is domain logic that keeps the entity valid.
Product.reserve throws InsufficientStockError when the quantity is more than the stock. This is a core business rule.
Product.release and the private assertQuantity method are pure state changes with checks on the entity. There is no I/O, persistence or framework code.
The only import is DomainError and InsufficientStockError from ./errors, which is in the same domain layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/product.ts is a pure domain entity. The Product class protects its own invariants: the id and name must not be empty, stock must be a non-negative integer, and quantities must be positive integers. It also holds the business rules for reserving and releasing stock, and it raises domain errors. The file has no persistence, transport, framework, presentation or orchestration logic. It only imports domain error types from the same layer. Every responsibility in the file fits the domain layer.
